purpose: The feature-by-feature matrix under the plan cards on Pricing: one column per plan with its name and action button pinned in the header while the page scrolls, one band per product with an overline, a title and a lead, and one row per feature saying what each plan includes — an included mark, a not-included mark, or the allowance as text. The recommended plan carries an accent bar, and below the large breakpoint the table folds to one plan picked from a searchable select. It is a page section — the site places it from a `{ _id: 'plan-comparison-section', props }` entry and binds `props` straight onto it — and it composes `module`, `select`, `input`, `button`, `hint`, `tooltip`, `eyebrow`, `tag` and `link`.
useWhen: Use PlanComparisonSection for a feature matrix across plans or support tiers: on Pricing under the plan cards, product by product, and on Support with one column per support tier.
avoidWhen: To compare Azion with one competitor → use `competitor-comparison-section`.
For price cards with a billing-period toggle → use `pricing-plans-section`.
related: `pricing-plans-section` — the plan cards this matrix sits under.
bestPractices: Give every plan a stable `id`; the narrow-screen picker selects by it.
Mark one plan `highlighted`; it gets the accent bar, the secondary button and opens the picker.
Give every row's `values` one entry per plan, in plan order.
Use a row's `hint` to define the term its label names; it opens in a `hint` note beside the label, so it can run to a sentence or two.
Set `includedLabel` and `excludedLabel` to the page's words; left empty, the marks read the locale's Included and Not included.
